chunks: Ahmad ibn 'Abdun narrated to me from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Zubayr, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Abu Hammam, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
Fasting the Day of 'Arafah is equivalent to a year [of fasting], and he said: Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) did not fast it, but Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) fasted it.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting on the Day of 'Arafah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar establishes the immense spiritual merit of fasting on the Day of 'Arafah, equating its reward to that of a full year, a status widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence. It further highlights the scholarly nuance of the practice by contrasting the consistent observance of Imam Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) with the non-observance of Imam Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), suggesting that while virtuous, it may not have been a strictly obligatory or permanent Sunnah for all Imams. This distinction invites deeper reflection on the flexibility of devotional acts within the Ahl al-Bayt's tradition.
